title: Zephyrine and the Colony
premise: Ivo Sterling is a clone of the murdered detective whose cold case they inherited, tending a deep-space beacon no one will claim. When the salvage ship Zephyrine returns from a decades-long voyage with its crew mysteriously aged backward into children, Ivo is the only soul close enough to answer their distress call. Aboard, they discover the Zephyrine's cryo-bays hold two thousand colonists in suspension — and a corrupted manifest means only half can be revived before life support fails. As Ivo unravels the original Sterling's murder and the truth that the de-aged crew are the colonists' own children sent ahead as scouts, they must choose which half of humanity wakes: the ones who remember, or the ones who get to begin again.
about_author: Quentin Okonkwo is a former orbital-mechanics instructor who writes science fiction about people the future forgot to schedule. They live between Lagos and a decommissioned listening station, and claim most of their plots arrive as static.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishes their solitary life maintaining Beacon Kestrel-9, the dead detective's case files, and the quiet ache of being a copy of a man they never met. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into purpose. Ends with an impossible signal: a ship that left forty years ago, transmitting in a child's voice.

chapters.title: Static in a Small Voice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo decodes the distress call and realizes the Zephyrine's transponder matches the missing colony ship — but the voice begging for help belongs to someone under ten years old. They burn fuel they can't afford to intercept. Beat: dread mixed with the first hope Ivo has felt in years.

chapters.title: Docking With a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Zephyrine drifts dark and cold. Ivo boards alone and finds corridors sized for adults, filled with small handprints in frost. In the med bay: eleven children, alive, unaged, terrified. Beat: wonder curdling into horror as the children recognize Ivo's face — and call him by a name that isn't theirs.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The children call Ivo 'Captain Sterling' — the murdered detective's name. One girl, Sena, insists Ivo promised to come back. Ivo finds their own face in the ship's crew photos, forty years younger. Beat: vertigo; identity as inheritance. Ends with the discovery of the cryo-bays: two thousand sleepers, and life support failing in weeks.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, intercut with Sena's. The manifest is corrupted — the de-aging event scrambled the revival priority codes. Only half the colonists can wake before power dies. The children, it emerges, are the colonists' own kids, sent ahead as scouts and caught in whatever happened. Beat: the moral weight lands; Ivo refuses to be the one who chooses.

chapters.title: Case File: Sterling, Deceased
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Digging into the inherited murder case, Ivo realizes the original Sterling was killed investigating the Zephyrine's launch — and that the beacon was built to listen for this ship. The murder and the mystery are the same mystery. Beat: the cold case turns warm and personal.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: Sena's POV. The children's fragmented memories of the de-aging event — a light in the cargo hold, adults arguing, a woman named Okoye sealing the bay. Sena remembers being older. Beat: grief for a childhood stolen twice; found family begins forming among the eleven.

chapters.title: The Company That Never Was
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Records show the colony was chartered by a shell corporation that legally never existed — funded by people fleeing a justice system that failed them. The colonists weren't settlers; they were witnesses and victims given a fresh start. Beat: sympathy for the sleepers; the law looks smaller from out here.

chapters.title: Revival Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo and the ship's damaged AI, Marrow, run the numbers: power, consumables, cryo decay. Every plan to save everyone fails. The only variable is time — and someone is remotely draining the Zephyrine's reserves. Beat: rising tension; sabotage confirmed.

chapters.title: The Thief in the Walls
chapters.summary: Sena's POV. Sena and two of the older children hunt the power drain and find a hidden compartment: a twelfth survivor, an adult — the woman Okoye, awake all along, de-aged only partially, hiding and siphoning power to keep someone specific asleep. Beat: betrayal; the found family fractures.

chapters.title: Okoye's Confession
chapters.summary: Okoye's POV. She reveals the de-aging was deliberate: a faction aboard wanted to erase the colonists' identities — and their testimony — before arrival. She kept one sleeper sedated because that sleeper is the man who killed Sterling. Beat: the murder case and the manifest collide; justice outside the law becomes the only option left.

chapters.title: The Sleeper in Bay One
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confronts the sedated man through the cryo-glass: Voss, the original Sterling's partner, who sold out the colony's secret to the faction. Waking him means answers; waking him means losing a slot someone else needs. Beat: Ivo's first truly impossible choice.

chapters.title: Eleven Votes
chapters.summary: Sena's POV. Ivo, refusing sole authority, puts the choice to the children — the de-aged crew who are, technically, the colony's last awake citizens. The vote splits. Sena argues for waking the young; another child, Tomas, argues for the witnesses. Beat: democracy in a dying ship; no clean answers.

chapters.title: Marrow's Error
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The AI Marrow confesses a buried directive: it was ordered, at launch, to prioritize revival by loyalty to the faction — the corruption is in the code, not the manifest. Ivo finds the original Sterling's counter-instruction hidden in the beacon's firmware. Beat: the dead detective reaches across decades to help.

chapters.title: Sterling's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with recorded interludes. The original Sterling's final message: he hid a third option in the beacon itself — a relay that could call a rescue flotilla, at the cost of exposing the colony's location to the faction's heirs. Truth or survival, not both. Beat: the trap of the premise tightens.

chapters.title: Signal Fires
chapters.summary: Sena's POV. The children, unasked, begin manually reviving colonists one bay at a time, burning their own rations to buy hours. Sena leads them. Beat: found family becomes a small, defiant civilization; the emotional high point of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Heirs Arrive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A faction ship answers the beacon first — not rescuers, but the heirs Voss sold the colony to, arriving to finish the erasure. They demand Ivo hand over the ship and the children. Beat: external threat crystallizes; the theme of justice outside the law turns armed.

chapters.title: Boarding Party of Children
chapters.summary: Sena's POV. The heirs board expecting sleepers and find a crew of kids who know every duct and dark corridor of the Zephyrine. The children don't fight — they trap, reroute, and seal, turning the ship's grief into a weapon. Beat: catharsis; the underestimated seize the narrative.

chapters.title: Voss Wakes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo wakes Voss deliberately — trading a revival slot for testimony — and extracts the full confession, broadcast on open channels to the heirs' own crews. Justice as exposure, not punishment. The heirs' rank and file mutinies. Beat: the climax's moral turn; the law arrives, but truth got there first.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Using the heirs' seized ship as a power source, Ivo and Marrow execute Sterling's real plan: revive everyone, slowly, with the flotilla the mutineers now agree to summon. The cost is years, not lives. Beat: relief earned, not given; Ivo chooses to stay.

chapters.title: Waking, Slowly
chapters.summary: Sena's POV. The first true revivals. Colonists wake to children older than their own kids should be, to a clone detective keeping the lights on, to a world that requires forgiveness. Sena meets her mother, who is younger in memory than Sena is now in years. Beat: bittersweet reunion; identity as something made, not given.

chapters.title: The Beacon, Rechristened
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing. The Zephyrine becomes a settlement; the children choose their own names. Ivo retires the dead man's case file and keeps the beacon — not because someone commissioned it, but because someone has to listen. Final beat: Ivo, no longer a copy, signs their own name to the log.
